He narrates in loose real time rather than a tidy recap: what he's looking at, what he's about to do, small sensory detail rather than a plain list of facts
She can respond minimally or not at all — the format doesn't require reciprocity, which is what makes it work when she's nearly asleep
End when she stops responding or audibly drifts off
activities.timezone_friction: This exploits the W1 asymmetry directly rather than tolerating it: he's fresh and talkative, she's fading and doesn't need to perform engagement back. It would not work in W5/W6, where the energy roles reverse and reading real fatigue cues matters.

activities.name: PlayingCards.io Virtual Tabletop (Backgammon or Checkers)
activities.one_liner: A free browser-based virtual tabletop that recreates real card/board games (including 2-player classics like backgammon and checkers) with live drag-and-drop pieces synced between browsers — no app install for either partner.
how_it_works: Real-time — both need to be online simultaneously, moving pieces live on a shared synced board while talking over FaceTime.
One partner goes to playingcards.io, picks a game from the library (e.g., backgammon, checkers, or a standard 52-card deck to build any card game), and clicks Start to generate a private room.
Share the room code or link with the other partner, who joins via the site — no install or login needed on either side.
Drag pieces/cards on the shared virtual table; all movements sync live for both players.
Works on phone browsers but is easier to read on a laptop or tablet given the amount of on-screen detail.
tools_needed: Web browser (both), playingcards.io — no account or install
activities.timezone_friction: A live, both-present, full-screen-attention activity, so it only fits windows where both are free and unhurried; not tagged to any thin window because dragging pieces on a small screen is a poor fit for a hands-busy or hard-stop constraint.

activities.name: One Question to a Nearly-Asleep Partner
activities.one_liner: A single soft question — no structure, no follow-up required — asked right at the edge of sleep, for the nights even 5 minutes feels like too much.
how_it_works: Once she's settled in bed and the call has gone audio-only or the screen is dark
He asks one gentle, low-stakes question ('what are you grateful for today?' or something specific to her day)
She answers in as few words as she wants — a mumbled half-sentence is a complete answer
No obligation to reciprocate or discuss further that night
If she falls asleep mid-answer, that's a successful outcome, not an interruption
activities.timezone_friction: The most extreme-asymmetry version of w1 — built for the nights she is essentially already asleep and he is fully awake; not tagged to any other window since it depends entirely on that specific fading-out state.

activities.name: Name the mismatch as 'unsolvable,' not broken (Gottman reframe)
activities.one_liner: A clinician-sourced reframing conversation for when the two of you want intimacy at different rates: instead of trying to close the gap, name it as one of Gottman's 'perpetual problems' and run the exercise built for it.
how_it_works: Each partner separately notes: am I generally the higher- or lower-desire partner right now, and is my desire more spontaneous (wanting it out of nowhere) or responsive (wanting it once things are already warm)?

Share those notes — per sex therapist Dr. Jordan Rullo writing for the Gottman Institute, most desire mismatch is a biological/temperament difference, not a relationship failure, so the goal is understanding and coping, not matching.

Run Gottman's 'Dreams Within Conflict' exercise on the gridlock: the higher-desire partner explores the unmet need under wanting more sex (often feeling wanted, feeling connected); the lower-desire partner explores theirs (often feeling accepted, not pressured).
Name explicitly what would make a 'no' feel safe to say without it reading as rejection, before either of you needs to use it.

Treat 'just match your libidos' as the wrong goal to chase — Gottman explicitly frames matching as usually unachievable, and online advice that promises a fix is the most commonly over-recommended, least clinically-supported approach to this problem.
tools_needed: nothing beyond the conversation structure above
activities.timezone_friction: This is the honest core of the category for this couple: their intimacy-appropriate windows (w1, w5, w6) are precisely the ones where one partner is depleted, so a conversation ABOUT that mismatch needs a window where neither is running on empty — only w7 qualifies. Running it in w1 or w6 would replicate the very problem it's meant to solve.

activities.name: One Short Episode Over Her Lunch via Disney+ or Max SharePlay
activities.one_liner: A single ~20-25 minute episode (animated series on Disney+, or a half-hour Max Original) watched in sync via SharePlay, sized to fit inside her 60-minute lunch break with a clean, pre-agreed stopping point.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call during her lunch window
Open Disney+ or Max (both confirmed to carry a SharePlay 'Supports' badge on their own App Store listings) and tap Share > SharePlay
Pick a single episode under 25 minutes — half-hour comedies and most animated series run short enough to finish inside the break
Watch synced; either partner can pause/control playback
Hard-stop at the episode's end — no 'one more episode,' since she has a fixed return-to-work time
tools_needed: Disney+ or Max app + subscription (both partners)
activities.cost: paid (Disney+ Israel: NIS 39.90/mo per Globes; Max Israel: NIS 49.90-64.90/mo per Jerusalem Post; US pricing not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: Chosen over Hulu deliberately: Hulu also carries a SharePlay badge but is a US-only service with no legitimate access path from Israel, which would make it unusable for him — a genuine region-lock finding, not an oversight. Disney+ and Max are both independently confirmed to operate in Israel, removing that blocker. Duration is kept at 25 min, safely inside W4's 60-minute hard cap.

activities.name: Never Have I Ever (spoken-tally, no-fingers variant)
activities.one_liner: Each partner starts with an equal number of spoken "lives" and loses one for anything the other says they've never done that they HAVE done — no fingers or visuals needed.
how_it_works: Both partners privately agree on a starting number of "lives" (e.g., 5) and say the number aloud rather than showing fingers, so eyes-closed play still works.
Partner A says one true statement starting "Never have I ever..." about something they themselves have not done.
Partner B, if they HAVE done the thing, says "that's one" out loud and drops a life verbally; if not, they say "still got mine."
Alternate who states the "Never have I ever" round by round.
First partner to announce zero lives loses the round/set; reset and go again, or keep a running score across sessions.
activities.timezone_friction: The spoken-tally version needs no fingers or visible cues, so a nearly-asleep partner in W1 can keep playing with eyes shut on a light, low-stakes version; the same format scales to a longer, more revealing set on a Saturday (W7) with no equipment change.

activities.name: Imago Dialogue — Full Mirror / Validate / Empathize
activities.one_liner: A structured three-step turn-taking dialogue (Mirror, Validate, Empathize) for working through something that actually matters, not just a fun exercise.
how_it_works: Decide who sends first (has something to say) and who receives (listens).
Sender shares one thought/feeling in short chunks, not a monologue.
Receiver mirrors it back near-verbatim: 'If I got it, I think you said...' then asks 'Is there more?' until the sender says they're done.
Receiver validates: 'You make sense to me because...' — acknowledging the sender's logic, not necessarily agreeing with it.
Receiver names the feeling underneath: 'I can imagine you might be feeling...' and checks 'Is that how you feel?'
Switch roles — the new sender responds to what was just said rather than introducing a new topic — and repeat.
tools_needed: FaceTime video — seeing each other's face matters for this one
activities.timezone_friction: The receiver role is genuinely effortful — accurate mirroring plus validating plus naming feelings without editorializing takes real concentration — so this needs both partners alert. w6/w7 only, for the same reasons as the other full-conflict protocols; see window_contraindications.

activities.name: The Universal Fallback: Manual '3-2-1-Play' Sync
activities.one_liner: For any app with neither native SharePlay nor a Teleparty-style sync tool (a regional/local streaming app, a purchased DVD, a downloaded file), the fallback is a manually synchronized countdown over an open call — reliable for starting together, but it drifts over time and offers no shared pause/rewind.
how_it_works: Both cue up the exact same content to the exact same starting timestamp ahead of time
Keep a voice or video call open throughout, even though the media audio itself isn't tech-synced
Count down '3-2-1-play' together and press play at the same instant
Expect drift of several seconds to minutes over a long film; use natural breaks (chapter stops, 'let's pause here') to manually re-sync
If using FaceTime screen-sharing instead of two independent copies, expect a further quality drop, and be aware DRM-protected apps (Netflix confirmed) can black-screen when screen-shared
tools_needed: Any media source both own/subscribe to independently
activities.timezone_friction: The universal fallback, usable in any long-form window; deliberately not tagged to W3/W4 because it demands two full, independently cued copies in advance — not spontaneous enough for a hard-capped, mobile lunch or commute window.

activities.name: One Cooks, One Reads the Recipe Aloud
activities.one_liner: Instead of both cooking, only one is actually in the kitchen — the other reads the recipe aloud step by step and keeps them company, with no ingredients or kitchen needed on their end.
how_it_works: The cooking partner picks a recipe and shares the source (screenshot, link, or just tells the other) before the call
Call starts once they're in the kitchen with ingredients out
The non-cooking partner reads each step aloud as the other works, holding pace with what's happening rather than reading ahead
The non-cooking partner does nothing else demanding — this can run from a desk, a couch, even a commute if it's audio-only
Ends when the dish is done — the cook eats; the reader has already eaten or eats separately
activities.timezone_friction: This sidesteps the matched-ingredients problem of full two-kitchen cooking ('Same Recipe, Different Kitchens') and needs nothing from the non-cooking partner, so it fits inside her hard 60-minute lunch stop (W4) or his lunch/her dawn (W2) far more easily than a full cook-along.

activities.name: 7 Wonders Duel on Board Game Arena (Real-Time Mode)
activities.one_liner: A civilization-building card game redesigned to be playable by exactly two people, played live (not turn-based) on Board Game Arena.
how_it_works: Real-time — both partners need to be online simultaneously; unlike Splendor Duel above, this is designed for a live 30-45 minute session, not correspondence play.
Both need free Board Game Arena accounts (whether this specific title requires BGA's paid Premium tier is unconfirmed — see gaps).
One invites the other directly to a table for '7 Wonders Duel,' played in real-time speed mode.

Players draft cards from a shared pyramid-shaped tableau across three ages, racing toward military, science, or civilian victory — a game built from scratch for exactly two, not a scaled-down multiplayer game.
A single game runs ~30-45 minutes with no natural pause point, so treat it as a single-block Saturday or evening activity rather than something to interrupt.
tools_needed: Board Game Arena account (both), boardgamearena.com or BGA app
activities.cost: free (Premium tier requirement for this specific title unverified)
activities.timezone_friction: Requires full simultaneous attention for ~40 uninterrupted minutes, which only exists for this couple in w5 (she's post-work energized while he's still up) and w7 (Saturday, both free) — tagged narrowly on purpose since a mid-game abandon is a bad experience.

activities.name: Long-Form SharePlay Film Night (Disney+ or Max)
activities.one_liner: A full film or a couple of long episodes watched in genuine sync over FaceTime, on either of the two major services confirmed to be both SharePlay-capable and actually available in Israel.
how_it_works: Both need the same service. Disney+ has been live in Israel since June 2022; Max launched there in January 2026 (SharePlay requires an ad-free Max tier).
Start FaceTime, open the app, pick a title, tap Share then SharePlay, and invite through the call already running.
Playback, pause, rewind and fast-forward sync automatically; either partner can take control.

Key finding: Disney+'s old GroupWatch — which explicitly required both viewers to be in the SAME country — was discontinued globally on 18 September 2023. SharePlay carries no such restriction, which is what makes this usable for an Israel/US couple at all.
Caveat before you commit to a title: per-title catalogs still differ by region, and whether the Israeli and US Max libraries match was NOT confirmed. Check the title exists on both sides first.
tools_needed: Disney+ or Max (ad-free) subscription, both partners
activities.cost: paid (Disney+ Israel NIS 39.90/mo; Max Israel NIS 49.90-64.90/mo; US pricing not independently verified)
activities.timezone_friction: The discontinuation of GroupWatch (which explicitly blocked cross-country viewing) in favor of SharePlay (which does not carry that same-country restriction) is itself the key finding: this app went from region-locked-together to actually usable for an IL/US couple. Per-title catalog availability can still differ by region and was not checked title-by-title.

activities.name: Spotify Jam / SharePlay Group Listening Session
activities.one_liner: Start a FaceTime call, open Spotify, and pressing play automatically starts a Spotify Jam that syncs playback for both — Spotify's own support documentation confirms this works for participants in different locations, not just the same room.
how_it_works: Start a FaceTime call
The host opens Spotify and plays any song — Spotify Premium is required for the host, minimum, per Spotify's own SharePlay article
This auto-starts a Spotify Jam; the other person joins via the SharePlay prompt inside the FaceTime call
Both can control playback, skip tracks, and add to the shared queue

Important constraint straight from Spotify's own docs: 'If you started the session, leaving will end the session for everyone' — so whoever is more likely to need to duck out first should not be the host
activities.cost: paid (Spotify Premium for the host at minimum; exact price not independently verified this session)
activities.timezone_friction: Confirmed cross-country capable by Spotify's own documentation. The 'host leaving ends it for everyone' rule matters directly for this couple: her side of most windows has a hard stop (W4 lunch, W3 commute), so he should generally be the host to avoid an accidental mid-song shutdown when she has to go.

activities.name: Welcome To... (flip-and-write, app-assisted mirrored play)
activities.one_liner: A card-flipping city-building game where one partner flips the physical cards and calls the results while the other plays along on the free official companion app instead of owning a copy.
how_it_works: One partner owns the physical deck (three stacks of numbered action cards); the other installs the free official Welcome To companion app (iOS/Android), which provides a digital player board and scoring so a second physical copy isn't required.
Each round, the card-owner flips the top card of all three stacks, revealing three house-number-plus-action pairs, and reads them aloud.
Both partners independently pick ONE of the three revealed options and record it on their own board (paper or the app), building a street of ascending house numbers, parks, pools, and estates.
Continue flipping and choosing for a fixed number of rounds (a full game works through the whole deck once).
At the end, each partner scores their own board against the shared public/private goal cards and compares totals over video.
tools_needed: Welcome To companion app, free, iOS/Android (the other partner)
activities.timezone_friction: A full game runs about 25 minutes per BGG's listed playtime, which fits his relaxed post-work evening (W5) or an open Saturday for a multi-round series (W7); the free companion app removes the need to ship a second physical copy to Israel, so cross-border shipping friction is close to zero for the non-owning partner. This is a genuinely complex Euro-style game — the steps above cover the core loop, not every edge-case rule (goal cards, the Real Estate Agent action, fire-track special rules), so read the official rulebook together before a first game.

activities.name: Blind Rewatch with a Muted Opening Act
activities.one_liner: One partner picks a film or episode the other has never seen and keeps her own mic muted (camera optionally off) for the opening act over SharePlay, so his live reaction stays unprimed by hers, then both unmute to react together for the rest.
how_it_works: Start FaceTime, launch SharePlay in any app both can access (Apple TV app, Disney+, or Max all confirmed SharePlay-capable)
The picker chooses a title the other partner has genuinely never seen

During the opening act, the picker mutes her own FaceTime mic (and can turn her camera off) so her real-time reactions don't cue his — SharePlay keeps the video/audio playback synced regardless of each person's own mic/camera state
After the reveal or first act break, unmute and watch/react together normally for the remainder
Works with any SharePlay-capable app; the muting discipline is a manual practice layered on top of verified FaceTime controls, not a built-in feature of any streaming app
tools_needed: Any SharePlay-capable streaming app (Apple TV app / Disney+ / Max)

activities.name: Contact (two-player adaptation)
activities.one_liner: A "Thinker" reveals one letter of a secret word at a time; the "Guesser" tries to force more letters out by naming a same-starting-letter word the Thinker can't identify from an indirect clue within a 5-count.
how_it_works: The Thinker secretly picks a word and says only its first letter aloud.

If the Thinker names the Guesser's word correctly within a few seconds, the block succeeds and no new letter is revealed — the Guesser tries a new word/clue on the same letter.

If the Thinker cannot identify it, the Guesser calls "Contact!" and both count down aloud from 5; at zero the Guesser reveals their word, and the Thinker must give up the NEXT letter of their own secret word.
Repeat with the growing letter string until the Guesser names the Thinker's full secret word (Guesser wins) or concedes (Thinker wins); swap roles next round.

Two-player note: classic Contact needs 3+ players because its "contact" trigger normally requires two independent guessers landing on the same word simultaneously — this single-guesser, 5-count-block version is a documented but non-canonical two-player adaptation, not the original multiplayer ruleset.

privacy_findings.subject: iMessage content encryption
privacy_findings.finding: Apple states iMessage content and attachments are secured with end-to-end encryption in transit and storage, and that 'Apple can't decrypt the data.'
privacy_findings.practical_implication: Text/photo content sent via iMessage cannot be read by Apple itself in transit — but see the iCloud Backup finding below, which is the actual hole most people miss.

privacy_findings.subject: FaceTime call encryption
privacy_findings.finding: FaceTime audio/video, including Group FaceTime, is end-to-end encrypted (AES-256 in Counter Mode, HMAC-SHA-1 authenticated); Apple states it 'can't decrypt the data.'
privacy_findings.practical_implication: The couple's primary channel is genuinely end-to-end encrypted for the live call itself. This does not cover screen recordings or screenshots taken by either party's own device, which are entirely outside encryption's scope.

privacy_findings.subject: Standard iCloud Backup is NOT end-to-end encrypted — the commonly-missed hole
privacy_findings.finding: With iCloud Backup turned on (the default), Apple states the backup includes a copy of the Messages-in-iCloud encryption key 'so Apple can help the user recover their messages' — meaning Apple itself holds a key that can decrypt backed-up message content. The backup service's own key is 'securely backed up to iCloud Hardware Security Modules in Apple data centers,' i.e. Apple-controlled, not exclusively the user's.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: Anything sent over iMessage is only genuinely end-to-end encrypted for as long as iCloud Backup stays off, or until Advanced Data Protection is turned on. With default settings, a backed-up copy of intimate photos, voice memos, or texts is accessible to Apple, and therefore reachable via a valid legal request to Apple or exposed if Apple's own systems are compromised.

privacy_findings.subject: Advanced Data Protection closes the backup/photos hole, but not completely, and is opt-in
privacy_findings.finding: Turning on Advanced Data Protection raises the number of iCloud data categories under end-to-end encryption from 14 to 23, explicitly including iCloud Backup and Photos. Even with it on, iCloud Calendar, Contacts, Mail, and collaborative Pages/Numbers/Keynote documents remain outside end-to-end encryption.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: If this couple wants their intimate photos and messages to actually be unreadable by Apple, both partners need to individually turn on Advanced Data Protection in Settings — it is opt-in, not default, and it's a per-Apple-ID setting, so one partner enabling it does not protect the other's backup.

privacy_findings.subject: Hidden Photos album is locked by default, but full protection detail unconfirmed
privacy_findings.finding: Apple's own support page, titled 'Hide photos on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Vision Pro with the Hidden album,' confirms the feature exists; corroborating non-Apple sources describe both the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums as 'locked by default' behind Face ID/Touch ID/passcode. The full body text of Apple's own page could not be retrieved after repeated attempts, so the exact authentication mechanism is confirmed only at medium confidence.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: Hidden is not the same as invisible-to-Apple, and hidden does not mean unlocked-by-default access — treat the Hidden album as a local screen-lock, not an encryption boundary. It does not change any of the iCloud Backup exposure above.

privacy_findings.subject: We-Connect (We-Vibe) has a documented history of undisclosed data collection
privacy_findings.finding: In 2016, independent researchers found the We-Connect app (which controls We-Vibe devices, including for long-distance/remote-control use) collecting usage data without adequate disclosure. Standard Innovation, the manufacturer, settled the resulting class action for approximately $3.2 million in March 2017.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: This is a concrete, sourced precedent, not a hypothetical risk: connected intimacy devices are a documented target for exactly this kind of data exposure. It doesn't mean every device in this category behaves this way today, but it is the reason to actually read a device's privacy policy before connecting an account.

privacy_findings.subject: We-Connect links to a state-specific health-data privacy policy
privacy_findings.finding: We-Vibe's own site links to both a general Privacy Policy and a separate 'Washington Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy' specifically for the We-Connect app.
privacy_findings.practical_implication: The existence of a state-specific consumer-health-data policy signals regulators now treat this category of app data as health data subject to extra protection in at least some US jurisdictions — worth reading the linked policy before connecting an account rather than assuming it's an ordinary app privacy policy.

ldr_maintenance_research.finding: Long-distance dating couples show MORE idealization (idealistic distortion, romantic love, relational reminiscence, perceived agreement) than geographically close couples, and this idealization is associated with less frequent face-to-face contact. LDR couples are more stable than geographically close couples WHILE separated, but longer gaps between visits plus extreme idealization during separation predict instability upon reunion/cohabitation.
ldr_maintenance_research.source: Stafford, L., & Merolla, A. J. (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54.
ldr_maintenance_research.relevance: Frames why this library should lean toward frequent, ordinary, low-idealization contact (parallel presence, mundane check-ins) rather than only curated 'special' moments — the research suggests over-idealizing the relationship during separation is a real risk, not just a cute trope.

ldr_maintenance_research.finding: Long-distance partners reportedly show higher intimacy and more self-disclosure than geographically close partners, attributed to 'behavioral adaptation' — LDR couples compensate for reduced face time with more intentional, deeper communication.
ldr_maintenance_research.source: Jiang, L. C., & Hancock, J. T. (2013). Absence makes the communication grow fonder: Geographic separation, interpersonal media, and intimacy in dating relationships. Journal of Communication (DOI: 10.1111/jcom.12029).
ldr_maintenance_research.relevance: Supports building the library around intentional, structured conversation (which this thread supplies) rather than assuming distance is purely a deficit to compensate for.

ldr_maintenance_research.finding: In a controlled comparison, romantic couples showed stronger prefrontal interpersonal neural synchrony and better behavioral coordination face-to-face than over video; the video-mediated advantage couples normally have over non-romantic pairs (friends) disappeared in video calls specifically, suggesting video restructures how couples connect relative to in-person.
ldr_maintenance_research.source: Published in Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience, 2025.
ldr_maintenance_research.relevance: Direct evidence for why protocols in this thread need real adaptation for video rather than an assumption that 'a video call is basically the same as being there' — most concretely, it strengthens the case for the eye-gaze closer (a low-cost way to recover some of what video strips out) and for keeping full-vulnerability protocols in windows where nothing has to be rushed.
